newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila shares end sharply higher in heavy volume.
newsitem.headline: Manila shares end sharply higher in heavy volume.

text.p: Manila shares finished sharply higher on Thursday, clawing back slight losses for the last two days on the back of a rise in blue-chips like PLDT, traders said.
"It seems like there was a short-lived consolidation phase and that the market is now resuming its run-up," said Bogart Cruz, trading manager at Asia Pacific Capital Equities Corp.
The main index closed up 31.67 points, or 0.97 percent, at 3,290.19 points.

"I think there's positioning of foreign funds on 1997 prospects of companies despite the negative news of an oil price hike. I think we will try to break through a major resistance of 3,400," said Spencer Yap, BPI Capital Corp research head.
Gainers beat losers 87 to 41 and 69 issues were unchanged. Volume was heavy at 9.5 billion shares valued at 2.929 billion pesos.
Aside from gains by index heavyweights PLDT and Petron, activity was focused on thirdliners on market talk of buy-ins and backdoor listings, traders said.
The Philippine Stock Exchange had to freeze the share price of three tertiary issues after their prices gained by close to 50 percent.
"There seems to be rotational buying where everyday a new issue is being strongly bought," said Teresa Lee, assistant vice-president at Lippo Securities.
Irving Ackerman, president at I. Ackerman & Co, said the market will likely sustain its uptick on Friday unless there are major changes on Wall Street or in PLDT in New York.
